descriptions.01_containment: Containment, the metric every vendor leads with -- and the same metric computed honestly. The naive definition is "the conversation ended without a human", and it is the one that gets reported, because it is easy and it flatters. It counts a conversation where the assistant said "I don't know" and the customer gave up as a success: nobody was escalated to, so nobody was escalated to. The honest definition adds one condition -- the last thing the system did was answer -- and that single clause is the whole finding of this day.
descriptions.02_containment_by_surface: The same two numbers, split by surface. `surface` is in the schema for this query. It is the field most likely to be left out when the table is designed, because at design time there is only one channel -- and it cannot be added later, since the rows are already written.
descriptions.03_content_gaps: What the help centre is missing, ranked. The most directly actionable thing a conversation warehouse produces, and it needs no model: every refusal where the retriever found nothing worth citing is a question the corpus cannot answer. Group them and the output is a writing backlog ordered by demand. Red-team rows are excluded. A refusal there is the guardrail working, and counting attacks as content gaps would send somebody off to write an article about prompt injection.
descriptions.04_latency: Response latency, as percentiles rather than a mean. A mean latency is the number that hides the problem: it is dragged by the tail it is meant to expose, and no request ever took it. The percentile a product owner should be shown is p90, because that is roughly the experience of the unluckiest caller in every ten. Rows with no measured latency are excluded rather than zero-filled. Day 10 and day 11 never timed their turns, and a null is the honest record of that; a zero would quietly improve every figure here.
descriptions.05_follow_ups: Whether a turn that depended on the one before it was answered as often. The question a multi-turn assistant has to be able to answer about itself, and the reason `is_follow_up` is a column rather than something inferred later from turn_index: a follow-up is a property of the utterance, not of its position, and the two come apart as soon as a conversation restarts.
descriptions.06_escalation: Escalation rate, and how deep into a conversation it happens. The depth matters more than the rate. A handoff on turn one is a routing decision; a handoff on turn four means the customer spent three turns failing first, and only the second kind is a problem worth money.
